h: A famous window and a starring role on screen
p: Here is a fact to impress your mates: one of the abbey's own windows features in the earliest surviving photographic negative. In 1835 Fox Talbot captured a small image of a latticed oriel window in the south gallery, and you can stand in front of that very window today. It is a tiny moment that changed the world, and seeing it in person is a lovely touch.

The Fox Talbot Museum by the abbey entrance explores his experiments and the early days of photography, so do not walk past it. It adds plenty of context and changing displays on photography old and new.

Lacock has had a busy screen career too. The abbey's cloisters were used as parts of Hogwarts in the early Harry Potter films, and the village has appeared in period dramas including the BBC's Pride and Prejudice and Cranford. Fans enjoy spotting familiar corners, and it gives younger visitors a fun reason to explore the cloisters.

Allow around three hours to see the abbey, museum and grounds, then add extra time for the village. Lacock is a popular spot, so arriving earlier in the day often means quieter streets and easier parking.

Nearby, Corsham, with its handsome high street and Corsham Court, is just a short drive away. Chippenham is close by for shops and places to eat, and Bath is near enough to combine if you are planning a longer trip in Wiltshire and Somerset.
